newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ireland's Bruton condemns IRA killing of policemen.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Bruton condemns IRA killing of policemen.

text.p: Ireland's outgoing Prime Minister John Bruton on Monday condemned the IRA's murder earlier in the day of two policemen in Northern Ireland.
"I wish on behalf of the Irish people to condemn the murders of John Graham and David Johnston," Bruton told reporters in Amsterdam, where he is attending a European Union summit.
"I think that this is deliberately provocative. They (the IRA) were seeking to provoke a reaction," said Bruton.

He was speaking after meeting British Prime Minister Tony Blair, who earlier denounced the IRA and its political wing Sinn Fein for the killings and said further meetings between Britain and the republicans were now out of the question.
The IRA, which is fighting for a united Ireland, had earlier claimed responsibilty for the point blank shootings of the two policemen in the town of Lurgan, southwest of Belfast.
Both Britain and Ireland have begun tentative talks with Sinn Fein in the hope of bringing about a new IRA ceasefire and reaching an agreement to end Northern Ireland's 28 years of conflict.

Bruton said he hoped his successor, Bertie Aherne, who won a general election earlier this month, would now also refuse to meet Sinn Fein officials. Aherne has pledged to hold such a meeting before he takes over as premier in late July.
"I would be appalled if he went ahead with a meeting in these circumstances," Bruton said.
